messages:
maria: Anyone else seeing model pulls fail in ap-southeast-1? Pods keep failing on image pull with "DNS lookup failed". Started ~09:05 UTC.
cheng: yep seeing it in monitoring, spike in DNS errors for s3-internal and registry.internal.svc.
alex: I see a ton of UDP truncation/errors from nodes. quick dig on one node: ```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
``` 
raja: @infra-bot did anything push to edge dns proxy recently? :thinking:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: edge-dns-proxy v2.3.1 rolled to ap-southeast-1 at 2026-03-18T08:58:12Z (staged) :rocket:
sam: interesting — we just had a conntrack increase change in the same cluster last night (nat helpers) to help GPU pools.
cheng: got `strace` on kubelet dns lookup showing repeated sendto/recvfrom with different src ports. looks like reply packets are landing on wrong socket when port space is tight. snippet:
```
sendto(3, "\...query...", 76, 0, {sa_family=AF_INET, sin_port=htons(53), sin_addr=...}, 16) = 76
recvfrom(3, "\...response...", 512, 0, NULL, NULL) = -1 EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable)
``` 
alex: this pattern matches: ephemeral source port reuse + UDP fragmentation/truncation -> upstream sets TC bit -> stub resolver shrugs and fails because TCP fallback not happening.
raja: edge-dns-proxy v2.3.1 enabled EDNS padding + EDNS client subnet by default (we thought would help caching). maybe upstream fwders can't handle EDNS and reply with FORMERR or truncation.
maria: logs from one proxy: `recvfrom: truncated packet, TC=1` and then `upstream fallback to TCP failed: connect: too many open files` — we might be hitting fd exhaustion on proxy.
alex: conntrack table shows high ephemeral usage. `conntrack -S` snapshot shows UDP entries ~120k and NAT ports cycling fast. suggestion: increase nat port range and reduce ephemeral reuse.
sam: mitigation ideas: rollback proxy to v2.3.0, disable EDNS features, enable TCP fallback in resolv.conf (options single-request-reopen?) and bump conntrack/ip_local_port_range temporarily.
cheng: opened INFRA-5342 to track root cause + postmortem. tagging oncall and infra. assigned to @raja.
raja: rolling edge-dns-proxy -> v2.3.0 now in ap-southeast-1. I'll also bump `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` on the node pool and increase `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` for GPU nodes.
maria: rollback started 09:11 UTC
alex: after rollback, image pulls recovered in ~3m. kube events show failures stop at 09:14 UTC.
sam: adding long-term fixes: (1) add TCP fallback for resolvers in our resolvconf helper, (2) add health check around proxy FD usage and failover to upstreams, (3) add e2e that simulates UDP truncation + conntrack exhaustion for modelfetch path.
cheng: notes for postmortem: include timeline, root cause (EDNS + proxy fd exhaustion + conntrack churn), mitigation (rollback, port range bump), and action items. will schedule PM for tomorrow.
raja: created a follow-up runbook entry and pinned it in #eng-infra. also added a temporary grafana panel for `edge-dns-proxy.fd_usage` and `conntrack.udp_entries`.
maria: thanks everyone. left a TODO to coordinate with network infra to test `tcp-only` fallback under load and to reach out to our forwarder provider about EDNS compatibility.
infra-bot: ticket INFRA-5342 updated: status=investigating, priority=high, owners=[raja, cheng] :spiral_notepad:
